name: Captivity
overview: The Scriptures reveal captivity as a divine judgment upon Israel for their disobedience, exemplified by God's promise to scatter them among the nations and allow their land to become desolate (Leviticus 26:33). This judgment was fulfilled when Israel was carried away to Assyria and replaced by foreign peoples (2 Kings 17:23-24), and Judah faced siege and exile in Babylon (2 Kings 18:9). Yet, captivity is also portrayed figuratively, as in Judges 5:12, where it signifies spiritual victory by leading captivity captive. Thus, captivity in the Bible encompasses both a historical punishment and a metaphor for redemption within God's sovereign plan.
